title: Reimagining Seventh-day Adventist Education: Moving Toward Neuro-inclusion for Autistic Learners
abstract: This article offers actionable, theologically grounded recommendations to help Adventist educators worldwide create safe, welcoming, neuro-inclusive spaces where autistic learners can flourish.

title: Write and Publish With Your Students
abstract: Sharing knowledge is one of the best ways to expand one's knowledge base and become a more effective practitioner. Writing for publication helps develop additional skills, such as the ability to analyze, synthesize, make critical judgments, and evaluate. When educators write and publish with students, they together contribute to building professional skills and advancing knowledge.

title: Seen, Known, and Formed: The Significance of Presence in Educational Leadership
abstract: Education begins with knowing. For teachers and educational leaders, knowing equals presence. In systems increasingly defined by efficiency, accountability, and performance indicators, are we truly present with those we are called to serve?

title: The Pathfinder Ministry: An Effective Method to Enhance Faith and Learning in Adventist Schools and the Community
abstract: This article discusses the philosophy and objectives of the Pathfinder Ministry and how it can complement the curriculum of Adventist schools. It also highlights the benefits of implementing community-based ministry.

title: What Matters Most: Students Speak About Faith Formation at School
abstract: The study reported on in this article examined students’ perceptions in three faith-based secondary schools in New Zealand to identify those aspects of the Christian school experience that they perceived as having the greatest impact on their faith formation.

title: Reflections on What Could Make a “Star” Chief Financial Officer in Church Organizations
abstract: One of the primary aims of Adventist educational institutions is to produce future church workers and finance professionals for the church. Five salient themes emerged as best practices and guiding principles for the finance professional committed to Christ: integrity, prudence in investing, accountability, fairness, and discipleship.

Fostering Emotional Intelligence in Children and Adolescents
abstract: Educators frequently see students with mental, emotional, and behavioral disorders. In the United States, it is estimated that one in five children experiences one of these disorders, and worldwide, one in seven. Most of these go untreated. This article shares the development of a curriculum to address these concerns.

title: Essential Elements of Leadership Style That Contribute to Student Achievement
abstract: Although much research has recently addressed student achievement, most studies focus on factors that promote success. Few have explored which leadership styles have the biggest effect on student achievement. This article is based on a study that examined school principals' leadership styles and their impact on student achievement.

title: Suicide Awareness and Crisis Planning: Trauma Responsive Techniques for Educators
abstract: Material contained in this article addresses topics of trauma, suicidality, and traumatization. The authors address being trauma-responsive, with emphasis on suicide awareness. It is imperative that Adventist schools have plans in place for prevention, intervention, and postvention.

title: Beyond Cowboy Boots and M&Ms®: Growing as an Education Professional
abstract: The concept of continual learning is not new, but for educators, it is essential, making professional development (PD) a continuous, lifelong process of acquiring new knowledge and skills.

title: GoEQ™ – Shaping Hearts, Inspiring Minds
abstract: Good teachers know that academic content is only part of what students need to thrive. Emotional health, resilience, and character play a critical role in success both inside and outside the classroom. That’s where GoEQ™ fills a need.

title: Rescuing Teachers From Burnout: Etiology, Symptoms, and Intervention Strategies
abstract: Burnout is ubiquitous within the teaching profession and can be detrimental to both the body and mind if educators are not vigilant in identifying its early signs and symptoms. This article provides helpful evidence-based suggestions for taking immediate action to preserve mental health and well-being.
